meta.title: Two Ways to Meet the Water

paragraphs: Posted by Lily. This week, Teacher Kim gave the Explorers two short texts about boats. The first text is an email from Grace, our pen pal in Singapore. The second text is my own report about our boat trip from the pier. Read them, and ask yourself what is the same and what is different.

Dear Lily, Last week, my class had a sailing lesson at a water sports center near our school. We went there by bus, and it took twenty minutes. Ms. Ong came with us, and so did two teachers from the center. Each boat was small and had one white sail. Two children sat in each boat, and my partner was a boy from my class.

First, a teacher showed us the equipment. We put on a life jacket and a hat, and we learned the names of the ropes. Then we sat in the boat and moved out on the water. The water was warm, and the teachers were kind. The wind was strong, so the boat moved fast, and we got wet. I was not afraid, and I want to try again. Do you go sailing in your town? Best wishes, Grace.

Our boat trip began at the pier on a Saturday morning. The pier was busy, and the sky was gray. The boat was big, and it had an engine but no sail. Twenty children and three teachers sat on long seats inside. The trip was delayed because the wind was strong. We waited at the pier for forty minutes, and Mia took photos of the waves. Then the boat driver said, "Come on board, everybody."

Before we sat down, the driver showed us the equipment. A life jacket was ready for each child, and Teacher Kim checked every one. We did not wear hats, because the boat had a roof. We did not sail the boat ourselves, however. Only the driver turned the boat, and we sat and looked at the water. The trip took thirty minutes, and we saw many birds on the waves. After that, the boat came back to the pier. Everybody said thank you to the driver.
Both texts are short, but each paragraph has a different idea. Read each paragraph again, and look for small facts. Which facts are the same, and which facts are different?
